comment: Accepted deviations of the oscillators of oscillators.lib and the antialiased functions of aanl.lib, see scripts/check_osc_claims.py; each entry gives the reason. `levels`: the aliasing measured, in dB at 44.1 and 96 kHz.

aa.acosh2.noise: second-order ADAA in float: its divided difference of divided differences cancels as consecutive inputs come closer at a higher rate, a noise floor that hides the suppression: -56.6 dB in -single against -70.4 dB in -double at 192 kHz (first order -67.8 dB in -single)
aa.acosh2.order: the input 3 + 2 sin reaches x = 1, where acosh' is infinite: the second order gains nothing there (-48.6 against -49.2 dB at 44.1 kHz); at 1.2 + 0.2 sin it gains 3.7 dB (-54.6 against -50.9)

aa.arctan2.noise: second-order ADAA in float: its divided difference of divided differences cancels as consecutive inputs come closer at a higher rate, a noise floor that hides the suppression: -71.7 dB in -single against -99.5 dB in -double at 192 kHz (first order -96.1 dB in -single)

aa.asinh2.noise: second-order ADAA in float: its divided difference of divided differences cancels as consecutive inputs come closer at a higher rate, a noise floor that hides the suppression: -71.2 dB in -single against -84.3 dB in -double at 96 kHz

aa.sinarctan2.noise: second-order ADAA in float: its divided difference of divided differences cancels as consecutive inputs come closer at a higher rate, a noise floor that hides the suppression: -75.5 dB in -single against -98.2 dB in -double at 192 kHz (first order -94.8 dB in -single)

os.lf_imptrain.sr: by design: one sample of 1 per period, so the mean is f0/SR and every harmonic falls 6 dB per doubling of the rate (an impulse of one sample, not of a duration)

os.oscb.noise: the biquad's coefficient -2cos(w) rounded to float: at 55 Hz at 192 kHz, -78 dB of non-harmonic energy (-162 dB in double)
os.oscb.tune-single: the biquad's coefficient -2cos(w) rounded to float sets the frequency: +2.6 cents at 55 Hz at 96 kHz (exact in double)

os.oscq.noise: the waveguide resonator fi.wgr rounded to float: its coefficient sets the frequency, -4.1 cents at 55 Hz at 192 kHz, and the recursion's rounding puts -69 dB of non-harmonic energy beside the sine (exact and -162 dB in double)
